episodes.211952: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across north central Oklahoma during the early afternoon of the 8th, along a cold front approaching the region from the northwest. The thunderstorms spread across eastern Oklahoma during the mid afternoon and evening. The atmosphere became moderately unstable during the afternoon ahead of the cold front in eastern Oklahoma, and deep-layer wind shear increased across the region with the approach of an upper level disturbance. The combination of moderately strong instability and strong deep-layer wind shear resulted in some thunderstorms evolving into supercell thunderstorms, the strongest of which produced large hail up to three inches in diameter and damaging wind.
episodes.212791: A stationary frontal boundary as well as both a Gulf of Mexico and Atlantic coast sea breeze combined with plentiful diurnal instability to produce robust thunderstorms across northeast FL during the afternoon and evening hours. Along with isolated severe thunderstorm activity, PWATs around 1.8 inches and slow moving/training convection resulted in very heavy rainfall and localized minor flooding.
episodes.213364: Scattered severe thunderstorms developed along a cold front across portions of northern and central Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 8th, spreading southward into southern Oklahoma and western-north Texas through the evening. Large to very large hail was the main storm hazard with several supercell thunderstorms during this time. Sporadic wind damage was also observed, including on the southwest side of the Oklahoma City Metropolitan Area.
episodes.213818: A frontal boundary south of Interstate 10 slowed and stalled near the coast while successive midlevel disturbances crossed the Lower Mississippi Valley. Deep moisture pooled along the boundary, with precipitable water values near 2 inches, supporting efficient rainfall and repeated rounds of thunderstorms. Morning storms produced large hail and damaging winds. Additional storms trained across portions of the Interstate 10 and 12 corridors, causing flash flooding in the Baton Rouge and Hammond areas. During the afternoon, stronger storms reached the New Orleans metropolitan area, lower Mississippi River parishes, and adjacent coastal waters, producing damaging winds, and large hail.
episodes.213819: A frontal boundary south of Interstate 10 in Louisiana slowed and stalled near the coast while successive midlevel disturbances crossed the Lower Mississippi Valley. Deep moisture pooled along the boundary, with precipitable water values near 2 inches, supporting efficient rainfall and thunderstorms that produced large hail and damaging winds in southwest Mississippi.
episodes.213820: A frontal boundary south of Interstate 10 slowed and stalled near the coast while successive midlevel disturbances crossed the Lower Mississippi Valley. Deep moisture pooled along the boundary, with precipitable water values near 2 inches, supporting efficient rainfall and repeated rounds of thunderstorms. During the afternoon, stronger storms reached the New Orleans metropolitan area, lower Mississippi River parishes, and adjacent coastal waters, producing severe wind gusts.
episodes.214075: A cold front stalled across the region while multiple short waves moved overhead. This produce multiple days of unsettled weather.

episodes.214423: On May 7th, the combination of daytime heating, the sea breeze convergence and the proximity of an upper-level trough produced strong showers and thunderstorms over portions of the Cordillera Central, leading to urban and small stream flooding in Ponce.

An NWS Storm Survey concluded that a widespread swath of wind damage extending from Bunkie to Plaucheville was the result of straight line thunderstorm winds occurring between 8:00 and 8:30 AM. There was widespread damage to trees and powerlines, including some snapped utility poles. Approximately 20 structures sustained damage, including partial roof removal of a home in Plaucheville. Based on the damage, wind speeds are estimated to have been between 60 to 90 mph.
